issues.title: notifications and full disk access catch up slower than the re-read behind refresh
issues.description:
`activate()` re-reads on the next main-queue turn, which is enough for the
fields the engine writes through a plain `DispatchQueue.main.async`:
accessibility, screen recording, camera, microphone.

Notifications and Full Disk Access do not settle that fast. Notifications wait
on `UNUserNotificationCenter.getNotificationSettings`, a round trip to a system
daemon; Full Disk Access is probed on a utility queue by listing protected
directories. Both can take tens of milliseconds, so the first frame after the
panel opens can show a stale value for them.

Harmless today: only accessibility and audioCapture gate a widget, and the
subscription corrects both of these when they land. It becomes visible the
moment a widget declares one of them in `WidgetDescriptor.permissions` — so
whoever wires the first such widget should read this first.

Found by the correctness review on ccp-ec8.

issues.title: bd makes its own git commits, and they bypass the commit-msg hook
issues.description:
Running 'bd dolt remote add' produced commit 815bc9b 'bd: update sync.remote' — authored as the user, not requested, touching .beads/config.yaml (it stripped the trailing newline, nothing more).

Two problems:
1. bd commits to git on its own. This repo's profile is conservative about git actions, and CLAUDE.md says not to commit without authority. A tool that commits as a side effect of a config read/write breaks that expectation silently.
2. The message names no bead. scripts/hooks/commit-msg would reject 'bd: update sync.remote' — the regex needs a ccp- id — so bd is committing with the hook bypassed. That is the same drift ccp-jze was filed for, except the bypass is not a human typing --no-verify, it is a tool doing it invisibly.

Nothing was harmed here; the commit is a one-character whitespace change. The concern is the mechanism.
issues.notes: Found while wiring the Dolt transport (ccp-0t2). Same class of issue as ccp-jze, which removed the --no-verify advertisement from the hook.

issues.title: workflow skill staleness gate is blind — context.py picks first tracks comment
issues.description: scripts/context.py:50 uses re.search for '<!-- tracks:' which finds the example comment at .claude/skills/workflow/SKILL.md:108 ('<!-- tracks: … -->') instead of the real tracks at :196. So lock entry is {'…': ''} and none of the 5 real sources (brief.sh, verify.sh, dashboard.py, hooks/commit-msg, context.py) are actually watched — e.g. editing scripts/hooks/commit-msg for ccp-jze did not trigger STALE as it should. issues.title: shim owns Combine->AsyncStream bridging that belongs in the adapter ccp-8ld.1 follow-up
issues.description:
`SystemPermissions.updates` builds an AsyncStream over `objectWillChange`,
which is a paradigm conversion, not a restatement of a type. The bridge rule
(Sources/VorssaintBridge/README.md) says a shim may restate but not decide,
and the taste review on ccp-8ld.1 flagged this as the one place the rule was
being stretched.

The shim should re-export upstream's publisher as-is — that *is* a
restatement, since Combine is the engine's native shape — and the adapter
should own the conversion and the lifecycle.

Landing with ccp-ec8: that bug needs the adapter to hold the subscription, so
the relocation is the fix rather than a tidy-up alongside it.
issues.close_reason: shim re-exports upstream's publisher as changes:; the Combine->async conversion and its lifecycle moved to the adapter

issues.title: Permissions updates buffers while panel is shut, leaks observation until next grant
issues.description:
`PermissionsAdapter.deactivate()` cancels the watch Task, but a task suspended
on `for await` over an AsyncStream is not woken by cancellation — the loop
only reaches its `Task.isCancelled` check when the next value arrives. So the
stream never terminates, `onTermination` never fires, and the Combine
subscription to `Permissions.shared` outlives the closed panel until some
permission changes and wakes the loop.

Idle CPU with the panel shut is a stated feature, and this is an observation
running against it. The buffering is the same fault seen from the other side:
AsyncStream defaults to unbounded, so yields pile up with nobody reading.

Fixing this needs deterministic teardown, which means whoever calls
deactivate() must hold the thing being torn down — the adapter, not the shim.
That makes this and ccp-bn9 one change.
issues.close_reason: adapter owns the subscription and cancels it synchronously in deactivate(); a shut panel now observes nothing

issues.title: the engine bridge, and the Permissions adapter
issues.description:
Every upstream type is internal, and VorssaintEngines is a separate module, so
nothing in the engine layer is reachable from CCPKit today. This bead
establishes the seam that unblocks the whole widget epic, and adapts the one
piece of shared infra v1 actually needs.

Sources/VorssaintBridge/ is compiled into the VorssaintEngines module
(sources: ["Vorssaint", "VorssaintBridge"]), so its files are module-mates of
upstream and can re-export internal types as public. It holds visibility shims
ONLY — no branch, no stored property, no decision. Anything that decides
belongs in a CCPKit adapter.

Originally scoped as "port seven files". Six of the seven turned out not to be
v1 work, and the survey is recorded on the bead rather than lost:

- BoundedProcessRunner needs no shim: its consumers (DiskSampler,
  PeripheralBatterySampler, NetworkProcessSupport, MaxCapacityProbe) are all
  inside the engines module. Transitive, invisible to CCP.
- Notifier has no v1 consumer — upstream UI/, WhatsApp, updates, cleaner, and
  MonitorAlertService, which is ccp-mlw.
- HotkeyManager + GlobalShortcut: v1's definition of done has no global
  hotkey. Deferred to its own bead.
- LaunchAtLogin: unblocked
issues.close_reason: VorssaintBridge compiled into VorssaintEngines as module mates, re-exporting Permissions as public PermissionSnapshot/PermissionKind/PermissionAuthorization and SystemPermissions. CCPKit's PermissionSource/PermissionsAdapter sits on the seam, mapping WidgetPermission to PermissionKind, exposing PermissionState and unmet set for inline grant, with activate/deactivate lifecycle that refreshes and watches via MainActor-isolated task. Deferred yield fixes stale objectWillChange read, nonisolated watch fixes deinit isolation, Equatable added, Package manifest silences 34 unhandled-file warnings by

issues.title: edit mode: wiggle, remove, and drag between lanes
issues.description: Long-press or an Edit button enters edit mode. Widgets wiggle via a small repeating rotationEffect with a random per-item phase offset so they do not sync, show remove badges, and become draggable. Prefer a custom drag gesture plus matchedGeometryEffect over .draggable/.dropDestination, which feel clunky for grid reordering. Drop targets: any position in any lane, plus an empty trailing lane that appears as a target to create a new lane.
issues.notes: lr7.2 owns PanelLayout.normalized() (prunes empty lanes, floors at one). Mutation verbs live here, and each must end in a normalized() call — that is what keeps the invariant without lr7.2 shipping the verbs. The trailing empty drop lane is a render-time affordance and must never be persisted. Reordering has to index around .unavailable slots, which are real positions in the lane.
issues.close_reason: Long press starts edit mode; per-card random period and head start for the wiggle; remove badges; live drag between and within lanes with the layout mutating under the finger. The new lane opens on the LEFT — the panel is right-pinned, so a trailing column shoves every card sideways mid-drag (built it trailing first and watched it). Verified by driving a synthetic CGEvent drag at the real window. Shipped in fb0038c.

issues.title: a panel taller or wider than the screen is cut off, not reflowed
issues.notes: ControlPanelController.sizeFitting clamps the panel to the visible frame minus the inset, so a layout with more lanes than the display can hold has its leftmost lanes cut by the window edge (the panel is anchored top-right). Same for a lane taller than the screen. Fine as a guardrail — five 240pt lanes need a 1300pt-wide display — but the real answer is either a horizontal scroll inside the panel, a cap on lanes with the overflow refused at drop time in edit mode, or a smaller lane width on small displays. Decide before edit mode lets anyone build a layout that wide.
issues.close_reason: Decided: cap, not scroll. Layout.laneCapacity(inWidth:) says how many lanes a display can show; edit mode refuses the drop that would exceed it rather than letting the arrangement grow off-screen. The existing sizeFitting clamp stays as the guardrail for a layout carried over from a wider display. A horizontal scroll was rejected — macOS Control Center never scrolls sideways and the panel is a control surface, not a document. Shipped in fb0038c.

issues.title: activate/deactivate lifecycle and idle CPU
issues.description: Sampling runs only while the panel is visible, except for widgets that explicitly opt into background sampling for a menu-bar stat. Enforced through activate()/deactivate(). Engine work off the main thread, models publish on main.
issues.close_reason: PanelArrangement owns the live widgets and starts/stops them with the panel; activation is idempotent there and in the sampler. SystemStatsWidget actually samples (1Hz) so the claim is testable. Measured 0.00s of CPU over 60s with the panel closed. The background-sampling opt-in from the description is NOT built — nothing needs it until the first menu-bar stat; see ccp-lr7.11. Shipped in 3242849.

issues.title: decide the layout save policy for edit mode: debounce and off-main
issues.notes: lr7.7 saves the layout after every drag mutation. JSONFileStore.save() is synchronous blocking I/O, so a naive save-per-mutation writes the file on the main thread mid-animation. Raised as an async-API finding by reviewer-taste on ccp-lr7.2 and declined there: the store is Sendable and actor-agnostic on purpose, so a caller can move it off-main, and making load() async would stop applicationDidFinishLaunching from having lanes ready when it builds the panel. The real decision is a save policy — debounce the writes and put them off-main — and it belongs with the mutation verbs, not the store.
issues.close_reason: LayoutAutosave: debounced 500ms, the write itself off-main, last layout wins, flushed synchronously when the panel closes or the app quits. Launch no longer writes the layout back at all — with every edit saved, a rewrite nobody asked for is a silent edit of the user's file. Shipped in fb0038c.

issues.title: panel dismissal: outside click and Esc
issues.description:
Dismiss on outside click via a global NSEvent monitor, and on Esc. The event monitor must be removed when the panel closes — a leaked global monitor is the classic version of this bug.

Multi-display placement was split out to ccp-lr7.10 and deprioritised.
issues.close_reason: Global mouse monitor for a click in another app, local key monitor for Esc; installed on show, removed on hide. Only the mouse watch is global so the status item's own click isn't seen twice. EventMonitors is a seam over NSEvent, so 'twenty opens and closes leave nothing installed' is a test. Shipped in 7ee672b.

issues.title: lane layout with placeholder widgets
issues.description: Vertical lanes stacking widget cards, driven by the layout model and rendering whatever the registry provides. Placeholder widgets only at this stage.
issues.notes: Also from lr7.2's review: JSONFileStore.load() returns whatever is in the file, un-normalized — the wiring here must call .normalized() on it before rendering. And see ccp-pr6 (duplicate ids in a lane) before ForEach-ing [LaneSlot].
issues.close_reason: Launch loads layout.json through JSONFileStore, normalizes, resolves against the registry and writes back; ControlPanel renders [[LaneSlot]] and draws UnavailableWidgetCard for an id this build lacks. Verified by hand-editing the file with a duplicate, an empty lane and an unknown id and relaunching: dedup and lane-closing applied, the unknown widget drew as a card and survived the round trip. Panel clamps to the visible frame — the clipping that clamp causes is ccp-p6g, and the capture proving it is owed (display was locked). Shipped in 7959c69.

issues.title: a layout with the same widget id twice in one lane resolves to duplicate LaneSlot ids
issues.notes: LaneSlot.id is the WidgetID, so a lane listing the same id twice yields two slots with equal ids and a SwiftUI ForEach over [LaneSlot] renders undefined. Raised by reviewer-correctness on ccp-lr7.2, which declined to file it on the grounds that no mutation logic exists yet — but the path does not need mutation: PanelLayout.load() will happily return {"lanes":[["stub","stub"]]} from a hand-edited or partially-mangled file, and lr7.6 will ForEach it. Recommendation: fold dedup (keep first occurrence) into PanelLayout.normalized(), which is already the invariant-maintainer that prunes empty lanes and floors at one lane — same place, same call sites, no new concept. NOT done in lr7.2 because normalized()'s contract was agreed with laurel as exactly those two invariants and widening it was not mine to decide unilaterally. Cheap; do it before lr7.6 renders anything.
issues.close_reason: normalized() now places a widget at most once, first placement wins, across the whole layout — a lane emptied by the dedup closes up under the existing rule. Three tests in PanelLayoutTests. Shipped in 7959c69.

issues.title: layout model and persistence
issues.description: [Lane] where Lane = [WidgetID], Codable, persisted as JSON in Application Support. Decoding must survive a stored layout naming a widget the registry no longer has, without discarding the rest of the arrangement.
issues.close_reason: PanelLayout as plain lossless Codable data, normalized() for the empty-lane and one-lane-floor invariants, LaneSlot + WidgetRegistry.resolve preserving unknown ids as visible slots, and a generic JSONFileStore. 6 new tests; gate green

issues.title: glass card design system
issues.description: The CCPUI vocabulary every widget draws from: spacing scale, corner radii (continuous, ~16-20), thin-material card fill, 1px white-alpha stroke, shadow, type ramp, accent for active toggles. Matches macOS Control Center's language; borrows nothing from Vorssaint, whose design is trademarked.
issues.close_reason: CCPUI design system: Space/Radius/Stroke/Layout in Dimensions.swift, a deliberately tiny Palette (semantic aliases over four white/black alphas; everything else is a system colour), GlassCard as the surface and WidgetCard as what a widget writes. A widget is buildable with no spacing, radius or colour literal.

Raise build.sh to 14.4 alongside the identity rename.
issues.close_reason: Reframed: build.sh is upstream's and could not build this fork at all (it compiles the Vorssaint executable target, which our Package.swift patch replaced with a library). Rather than rewrite 631 lines of it, CCP got scripts/app.sh — twenty lines over SwiftPM, AppBundle/Info.plist for the identity, LSUIElement, 14.4 floor — plus scripts/capture.sh for design-review screenshots. build.sh left untouched; recorded in PATCHES.md.

issues.title: status item and non-activating glass panel
issues.description: NSStatusItem toggles an NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel, level .popUpMenu, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]. Real blur via NSVisualEffectView (.hudWindow or .popover, blendingMode .behindWindow) wrapped for SwiftUI. Anchored top-right of the screen holding the status item, width growing leftward with lane count up to full width. Pre-warm the window at launch.
issues.close_reason: Status item toggles a borderless non-activating NSPanel at .popUpMenu, canJoinAllSpaces, anchored top-right of visibleFrame (so an auto-hidden menu bar is not a special case). Window and SwiftUI graph built at launch and never torn down. Blur ended up per-card rather than per-panel at the user's direction: the window is transparent and each GlassCard carries its own behind-window NSVisualEffectView, because a panel-wide backdrop reads as a dark container and SwiftUI materials can't blur the desktop. Panel size comes from the hosting view's fittingSize.

issues.title: design the CCPWidget protocol and registry
issues.description: Everything hangs off this, so it comes first. CCPWidget with a static WidgetDescriptor (id, title, icon, default size, required permissions), makeView(), activate()/deactivate(), optional settings and compact/expanded variants. Plus WidgetRegistry listing what is available.
issues.close_reason: CCPWidget + WidgetDescriptor + WidgetRegistry in CCPKit/Widgets. Registry is composed by the app rather than a self-assembling shared instance, so tests stand up fixture registries; re-registering an id replaces it in place so gallery order stays declaration order. WidgetSize is a named enum in CCPKit and the points live in CCPUI. 10 tests.

issues.title: beads never export issues.jsonl — the ledger is invisible to git
issues.description: psymail-mini syncs its ledger by committing .beads/issues.jsonl alongside code; its origin has no refs/dolt/data, so git IS the transport. CCP has no issues.jsonl at all: .beads/config.yaml lacks the 'export: auto: true' block (and sync.remote), so bd never writes the export and every bead filed here is invisible to git and lives only in the local embedded Dolt DB. issues.title: README build instructions advertise a build that produces a Vorssaint bundle
issues.description: README.md:71-78 tells people to run ./build.sh and ./build.sh --install, but build.sh is upstream tooling that sets EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint and APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils (build.sh:27-36). The same README states CCP 'presents no modified build as Vorssaint', and TRADEMARKS.md requires forks to use a different name, icon and bundle identifier. So the README instructs the reader to do the exact thing the README and TRADEMARKS.md forbid. The underlying identity fix is ccp-v64; this bead is the README not advertising it in the meantime.
issues.close_reason: README's build section now uses 'swift build' and states plainly that build.sh still emits a com.vorssaint.utils bundle TRADEMARKS.md forbids a fork from shipping, pointing at ccp-v64 for the rename. Placeholder clone URL replaced with the real origin. Committed 3d28645.

issues.title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
issues.description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
issues.design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
issues.close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

issues.title: commits bypassed the commit-msg hook with --no-verify
issues.description: 3f01781, 6001d7f and ffb9bbc were all committed after 2897fe7 installed a working blocking commit-msg hook, and none names a bead — only --no-verify gets past it. Consider requiring a reason, or logging bypasses so the drift is at least visible.
issues.close_reason: removed the 'Genuinely unfilable? git commit --no-verify' hint from scripts/hooks/commit-msg:39-41 per option #1. skills.name: agentic-review

skills.name: handoff

agents.name: reviewer-design

agents.name: reviewer-taste

Reads a review packet and reports violations. Runs on a cheap model; use for every change worth reviewing.

nodes.role: Audits the whole knowledge layer at once — every skill, every memory, and what a session pays before it starts — and proposes what to merge, delete, shorten, or promote. Reads a digest rather than the repo. Run on a cadence or when the always-loaded cost climbs, never on the hot path of doing work.

nodes.name: reviewer-correctness
nodes.role: Hunts for real defects in a control-center-pro diff — logic errors, concurrency bugs, lifecycle and state mistakes, and the platform traps this project keeps hitting. Reads a review packet and reports only findings with a concrete failure scenario.

nodes.name: reviewer-design
nodes.role: Reviews screenshots as a principal design engineer — what the app actually renders, not what the diff says it should. Hunts clipping, truncation, overflow, misalignment, and drift from the app's established look. Reads a review packet listing captures to look at. Use whenever a change touches anything on screen.

nodes.name: reviewer-taste
nodes.role: Reviews a control-center-pro diff against the project's documented taste — composition, module size, naming, comments, accessibility. Covers the app and the harness scripts. Reads a review packet and reports violations. Runs on a cheap model; use for every change worth reviewing.
